_note: Deterministic canonical team names, for FINAL_2's identity rule ('normalized teams + competition + kickoff bucket'). Exact normalized string on the left, canonical normalized string on the right - there is no scoring, no substring test and no token overlap here, and nothing may be added on a hunch. A key is only written after the same real fixture has been observed published under both spellings AND an independent source has been checked, and the evidence is recorded beside it. Read by scanner/team_identity.py, which is the only place that loads this file; scanner/fixture_dedupe.py and scanner/merger.py both ask that module, so the tabs, the merge and the archive cannot disagree about who is playing.
_forbidden: No generic rule may be expressed here or derived from it: not 'drop United', not 'drop City', not 'drop FC', and not 'drop a trailing W'. Manchester United and Manchester City are two clubs and must never share a canonical name; a men's fixture and a women's fixture between the same two clubs are two fixtures. Each entry maps one exact spelling to one canonical name and affects nothing else.

_gender_scope: An entry may carry "gender": "women" (or "men"). A scoped entry is applied ONLY to a fixture whose own evidence - its title or its competition, read with scanner/schedule_resolver._gender - says the same thing. It is how 'Brighton W' can be canonicalised to 'Brighton' for a Women's Super League fixture without ever letting a women's fixture fold into a men's one. It is NOT a rule about the letter W: no suffix is stripped, and a spelling with no entry here is left exactly as it is.

_refused._note: Near-miss pairs this table deliberately does NOT relate. A near-miss agrees on one side and on the clock, which is strong evidence and not proof: two fixtures can share an opponent and an hour. Each refusal is kept so the next audit does not re-open it.
_refused.cricket highlights t20 asia cup 2026 pak: our side is a programme title the parser could not reduce to a team; the fix belongs in the title, not in an identity table.
_refused.dubai united -> united: "United" alone names dozens of clubs. A canonical name has to identify one.
_refused.garudayaksa -> pskc kota cimahi: two different Indonesian clubs, both of which played Persik Kediri.
_refused.llaneros -> atletico nacional: two different Colombian clubs. The census pairs them because both met Deportivo Cali at a matching hour - which is what a one-side rule cannot tell apart, and exactly why the table is not built from it mechanically.
_refused.nuremberg -> nurnberg: one club and two spellings, each of them a single word, so neither can be a key without breaking the rule that a bare word never is one. The evidence is real - LiveScore prints 1. FC Nuremberg for our 1 FC Nurnberg - and the mechanism to express it safely does not exist here.
_refused.oestersunds -> ostersunds: the same shape, and the same refusal. Note that oesters if / osters if IS expressible, and is in the table.
_refused.olimpia -> deportivo olimpia: CD Olimpia of Honduras and Olimpia of Asuncion are both spelled Olimpia in these feeds. Relating the bare word would give two clubs one canonical name.
_refused.platense -> atletico platense: Club Atletico Platense of Argentina and Platense FC of Honduras. Same reason.
